newsitem.title: UK: LME copper ends on highs, helped by wider spread.
newsitem.headline: LME copper ends on highs, helped by wider spread.

text.p: Copper prices picked up to finish near the day's highs comfortably above the $2,100 level on Wednesday, boosted by a widening backwardation, traders said.
Three-months copper finished the afternoon kerb on the London Metal Exchange (LME) at $2,114, up $19 from Tuesday and right up against the day's high of $2,115.
Brisk borrowing of the January dates, which some traders linked to expected tightness around the January options declaration, helped boost values, traders said.
January/threes widened from $41 on Tuesday to $65.
That activity also helped widen the cash to threes backwardation steadily throughout the day. It was last at around $90, up about $40 from Tuesday.
But business was patchy ahead of the Christmas holidays and traders said they expected copper to remain within its recent range barring unexpected news or surprise LME stock movements.
"It's basically range trading between $2,080 and $2,115," one trader said. "Business is slow and it's hard to imagine any fireworks right now."
The $2,080 level provided support for copper when the market bottomed out on Monday and Tuesday, and a breach would target $2,000, chartists said.
On the upside, significant resistance was seen at $2,130 and $2,150.
Aluminium also ticked higher on the back of copper, building on slightly stronger levels achieved on Tuesday.
It finished at $1,537, also near the day's highs, and up $7 from Tuesday.
Nickel continued a steady recovery from the 26-month lows touched on Monday. It was last near its highs for the day at $6,640, up $65.
Tin ended just $10 lower at $5,820 after easing following Tuesday's hefty bounce from 19-month lows hit on Monday.
Zinc was little changed at $1,053, down $2, while lead eased back below the $700 level to end $3 weaker at $698.
Alloy was last bid at $1,370, up $5.
